property_summary: For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and msg.value, after calling Put the contract's recorded Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp (the reference enforces unlockTime >= block.timestamp), whereas the mutant allows unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs and thus can violate this invariant.

For any caller, after calling Put(...), the reference guarantees Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp; the mutant that assigns _unlockTime directly can set unlockTime < block.timestamp, violating this invariant for some inputs.

After any Put call by any address with any _unlockTime and any value, the reference contract guarantees Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now), while the mutant that writes _unlockTime directly can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime — so the property is: Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp always.

For any caller and any inputs, after calling Put(...) the reference guarantees that Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp OR the call reverts; the mutant can accept a Put that results in Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime causing the invariant to be false, so we assert that Put never results in stored unlockTime < block.timestamp (i.e., post-call unlockTime >= block.timestamp).

For any caller, after calling Put(...) the reference contract always stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now); the mutant that assigns _unlockTime directly can store a past unlockTime (< block.timestamp) for some fuzzed _unlockTime, breaking this invariant.

After calling Put from any caller with any deposit and unlockTime, the caller's recorded balance in Acc[msg.sender].balance must equal the sum of previous balance plus the deposit (i.e., Put never leaves the contract in a state where the deposit was not credited); removing the nonReentrant_ guard allows a reentrant attacker to cause mismatch so that after Put completes the stored balance is less than the deposit added (the buggy mutant can be exploited via reentrancy).

After any single external Put call from any caller with any deposit and unlockTime, the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance is at least the sum of all deposits they made (i.e., Put is non-reentrant and never results in a final stored balance less than the funds sent); removing nonReentrant_ allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during Put so the final stored balance can be less than the deposit, violating this invariant.

For any caller, after a single Put(...) call that sends ETH, the contract's recorded balance for that caller (Acc[caller].balance) equals the prior recorded balance plus the sent value; removing nonReentrant_ allows a reentrant attacker to re-enter Put/Collect during the Put call and make the final recorded balance not equal prior+sent, so the buggy mutant can violate this invariant for some inputs.

Invariant: For any caller and any single Put(amount, unlockTime) call, if the callee called by Put (LogFile.AddMessage) does NOT revert and does not reenter, then after Put returns the contract's balance increases by exactly the sent amount and Acc[caller].balance >= sent amount; removing nonReentrant_ allows a reentrant attacker (a malicious LogFile that reenters Collect) to withdraw during Put so after Put returns the contract balance can be lower than the sent amount and Acc[caller].balance can be less than the sent amount.

For any caller and any single Put call that sends ETH, when the Log contract is malicious and re-enters Collect during Put, the reference (with nonReentrant_ on Put) ensures Put always completes without allowing reentrant withdrawals so that after Put returns the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance equals the contract's cumulative recorded balance addition (i.e., contract balance increases by the deposit and Acc[msg].balance >= deposit), whereas removing nonReentrant_ (the mutant) allows the malicious Log to re-enter and withdraw during Put causing the final stored balance or contract balance to be lower (the mutant violates this).

For every caller and value, the reference contract always records the Put event in Log.History with the same msg.value as the balance increment happens (i.e. after Put, History[last].Val equals the amount added to Acc[msg.sender].balance); the mutant that logs before updating balance can produce a mismatch between the logged Val and the actual recorded balance update ordering for some inputs.

After any successful Put by an address, the most recent Log.History entry's Val equals the increase in that address's Acc.balance (i.e., History[last].Val == delta balance); the mutant that logs before updating balance can make the recorded History.Val not match the actual balance increase for some inputs.

After any Put by an account, the reference contract always records the logged message's Val equal to the Ether value sent in that call and that same value is reflected in the account's balance increase (so reading Log.History[last].Val equals msg.value of that Put); the mutant that logs before updating balance can produce an observable mismatch for some inputs when external behavior interacts (we detect this by comparing the logged Val to the actual stored balance delta after Put).

For any caller and sent ether amount, after Put completes the caller's Acc.balance is at least as large as the last logged Put value for that caller (i.e., the recorded log value is never greater than the actual stored balance); the mutant that logs before updating balance can cause the log to record a value that appears to exceed the stored balance for some inputs involving a reentrant attacker that receives the log call and reenters to drain balance.

For any caller and sent ETH amount, after Put returns the reference contract guarantees that the newly appended Log.History entry's Sender equals the caller address (msg.sender); the mutant that calls LogFile.AddMessage before recording acc.balance can cause a reentrant attacker to become the observable msg.sender in the log (or otherwise misattribute the sender) for some inputs, breaking this invariance.

After a successful Put(...) call, the caller's recorded balance in Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by the exact msg.value (i.e. Put is additive and leaves c.Acc[caller].balance >= previous balance + msg.value); the mutated modifier that clears the lock before function body can allow the function to behave incorrectly so this invariant can be violated for some inputs (via reentrancy allowing nested Put to disturb balances).

The reference contract C is non-reentrant: for any caller and any amount, a direct call to Put(...) cannot be reentered during its execution (so a malicious receiver that attempts reentrant Collect during Put cannot steal funds or change c.balance as observed via address(c).balance), but the mutant that clears the lock before the body permits reentrancy and can change contract balance for some inputs.

For any caller, after a single external Put(...) invocation that sends Ether, the contract's total balance (address(c).balance) increases by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., Put cannot be reentered to change the contract-wide balance during its execution); the mutant that clears the lock before the body allows reentrancy and can cause address(c).balance to differ.

For any caller and any sent amount, after a single successful Put(...) call the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance is at least the amount they just sent (i.e., Put always increments the caller's recorded balance by >= msg.value); the mutant that clears the lock before the body permits reentrancy and can make Acc[msg.sender].balance not reflect the deposited amount for some inputs.

The reference C ensures that calling Put(...) with any caller and any nonzero ether amount cannot be reentered to trigger Collect during the same Put call (so Put always completes without a nested Collect that reduces the depositor's recorded balance), while the mutant that clears the lock before the body allows a reentrant attacker to invoke Collect during Put and thus can cause Put to finish with the depositor's recorded balance smaller than expected (observable via Acc[attacker].balance or address(c).balance).

After a deposit that meets MinSum, a single Collect call can never reduce the depositor's recorded balance by more than the collected amount (i.e., balance decreases exactly by the transferred amount).

property_summary: A direct call to Collect should not revert when the caller has sufficient recorded balance (>= _am) and unlockTime has passed and balance >= MinSum.
When caller's recorded balance is at least MinSum and at least the requested amount, and the unlock time has passed, calling Collect must not revert (reverted == false).
If a caller has balance >= MinSum and >= _am and unlockTime < block.timestamp, then Collect must not revert (i.e., reverted == false).

If the caller's balance is below MinSum, then Collect must either revert or not transfer funds (i.e., behavior may vary) — we assert that Collect reverts when caller's balance is strictly less than MinSum, requested amount >0, and unlockTime condition is irrelevant.

Invariant: After a successful Collect call, the caller's recorded balance in C (Acc(addr).balance) is decreased by the withdrawn amount; removing the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker to drain/alter balance so this rule can be violated.

For any caller and withdrawal amount, a successful single Collect call on the correct contract always reduces the caller's recorded Acc.balance by exactly the withdrawn amount (i.e., Acc(balance_after) = balance_before - amount); removing the lock allows reentrant calls during Collect to change the final recorded balance so this equality can be violated by an attacker.

For any depositor and withdrawal amount, a single external call to Collect(uint) cannot result in the contract's total recorded balance for that depositor decreasing by more than the withdrawn amount (the non-reentrant lock prevents reentrant extra deductions); removing the lock allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw extra funds so the property can be violated.

For any depositor, if their Collect call completes successfully when their withdraw amount is <= their balance and unlock time passed, then the caller's recorded balance (Acc(addr).balance) is strictly less than the balance before the Collect call (i.e., some amount was deducted); the mutant allowing reentrancy can make a single Collect call finish while leaving the recorded balance unchanged (or inconsistently changed) for some attacker inputs via reentrant drains.

For any depositor and withdraw amount, when Collect(...) returns successfully on the correct contract, the contract's public Acc(depositor).balance is strictly less than it was before the call (i.e., some funds were deducted); removing the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker to make Collect return successfully while leaving the recorded balance unchanged (or not decreased), so the property is violated for some inputs.
After one successful Collect that withdraws funds, a second Collect call by the same holder with the same amount must succeed (not be blocked by reentrancy lock).

Calling Collect once should not permanently cause subsequent Collect calls (with same caller and amount) to revert; i.e., Collect reverts only if preconditions (balance≥MinSum, balance≥amount, unlockTime passed) fail, so if those hold for the first call and it succeeds, a second identical Collect should also succeed unless preconditions changed by the first call's legitimate effects.

If a first Collect call by this contract's address with given _am does not revert, then a second immediate Collect call with the same _am must also not revert (i.e., Collect does not permanently lock out further calls by the same caller when initial call succeeds).
If the first Collect call by the same caller succeeds (does not revert), then a immediately following second Collect call with the same amount must also succeed (not revert).

If a caller's Collect call does not revert, then calling Collect a second time (immediately after) must also not revert when the caller still has enough balance to cover the same amount and unlockTime has passed and MinSum requirement holds.

For any caller and amount that previously allowed a successful Collect, the reference contract always unlocks the nonReentrant lock at the end so a subsequent Collect call from the same caller (with remaining balance >= MinSum and after unlockTime) may proceed; the mutant that omits resetting locked_ blocks all later Collect calls (non-reentrant lock never released), so some inputs produce a failing subsequent Collect while reference permits it.

For any caller, if they Put enough funds and time passes past their unlockTime then the first Collect and a subsequent Collect (after reducing amount) both succeed on the reference because the reentrancy lock is released, whereas the mutant that never resets locked_ will block the second Collect causing it to revert.

For any caller who has deposited at least MinSum and whose unlockTime has passed, two sequential successful Collect calls (first withdrawing some amount then a second withdrawal) are both allowed by the reference (because the nonReentrant_ lock is released), whereas the mutant that never clears locked_ will allow the first Collect but will block (revert) the second Collect.

For any depositor who has balance >= MinSum and whose unlockTime has passed, two sequential Collect(...) calls (with admissible amounts) both succeed on the reference contract (lock is released after each call) while the mutant that omits resetting locked_ causes the second Collect to revert, so the reference always allows the second Collect but the mutant blocks it for some inputs.

For any depositor that has previously Put >= MinSum and whose unlockTime has passed, the correct contract allows two sequential Collect calls (both complete) while the mutant that never clears the reentrancy lock causes the second Collect to revert for some admissible inputs.
After a successful Collect that sends _am to the holder, the holder's recorded balance decreases by _am (i.e. previous balance = new balance + _am).

If Collect call succeeds (does not revert) then the contract's ether balance decreases by exactly the amount transferred (i.e., address(c).balance decreases by _am), otherwise no change requirement — ensuring the contract's stored balance and actual ether flow stay consistent.
